claim.title: Boundary test: pN invariance of the Bayes Gap
claim.statement: For the small uniform-attention meta-learner used in the C2 audit, the Bayes Gap is approximately invariant to how a fixed pretraining budget is split between prompt count N and prompt length p, while decreasing monotonically with the product pN.  In other words, at matched values of pN the gap stays within a small relative band even as N and p vary.
claim.test_plan: Reuse the mean-pooling least-squares meta-learner from the C2 audit_attempt4.py setup.  Train on matched-pN pairs such as (N,p) = (100,20),(200,10),(400,5),(500,8),(1000,4),(2000,2),(1000,8) with several replicates per cell.  Estimate the Bayes Gap for each (N,p) by out-of-sample MSE minus the exact posterior-mean risk on fresh query points.  Report each Bayes Gap, fit a monotonic trend versus pN, and compute the within-pN coefficient of variation.  Also run a synthetic-data control where BG is generated from a known pN-only law.
claim.success_criterion: (i) Spearman correlation between Bayes Gap and pN across the full grid exceeds 0.80; (ii) the mean within-pN coefficient of variation is below 0.25; (iii) a positive synthetic control with a true pN-only law satisfies both (i) and (ii).
